644c1ce65ea5bc671f89ccc62fd35e036b7ba323.rationale: Temporal evidence of recent rapid ascent from a deep dive and presence of microbubbles in the right heart chambers support Decompression sickness

Decompression sickness: Glasgow Coma Scale score: 14, which is relatively high and may not fully support the severity of decompression sickness
Normal hemoglobin, platelets, glucose, ESR, creatinine, urea, potassium, sodium, and D-dimer
Valsalva maneuver–enhanced color‐flow Doppler study: no evidence of a patent foramen ovale, which might be expected in some cases of decompression sickness
Chief complaint: dyspnea, lethargy, severe generalized arthralgia, and mild confusion
Physical examination: bilateral joint pain worsened by movement without erythema or swelling
Vital signs: blood pressure 90/60 mm Hg
Vital signs: oxygen saturation 90% on room air
Transthoracic echocardiography: spontaneous echo contrast consistent with microbubbles in the right heart chambers
History of rapid ascent from a 50 m sea-depth saturation dive
